passage.text: Thanks for practicing your presentation with me today.
passage.reading: ˈθæŋks fər ˈpræktɪsɪŋ jʊr ˌprɛzənˈteɪʃən wɪð miː təˈdeɪ.

passage.text: You've improved a lot, and I'm sure you'll do well next week.
passage.reading: juːv ɪmˈpruːvd ə ˈlɑːt, ənd aɪm ˈʃʊr juːl ˈduː ˈwɛl ˈnɛkst ˈwiːk.

passage.text: Here are five tips to help you on the day.
passage.reading: ˈhɪr ər ˈfaɪv ˈtɪps tə ˈhɛlp juː ɑːn ðə ˈdeɪ.

passage.text: First, go over your slides several times before the presentation, but don't try to memorize every word.
passage.reading: ˈfɜːrst, ˈɡoʊ ˈoʊvər jʊr ˈslaɪdz ˈsɛvrəl ˈtaɪmz bɪˈfɔːr ðə ˌprɛzənˈteɪʃən, bʌt ˈdoʊnt ˈtraɪ tə ˈmɛməraɪz ˈɛvri ˈwɜːrd.

passage.text: Second, write short notes on cards, and look at them only when you need to.
passage.reading: ˈsɛkənd, ˈraɪt ˈʃɔːrt ˈnoʊts ɑːn ˈkɑːrdz, ənd ˈlʊk ət ðɛm ˈoʊnli wɛn juː ˈniːd ˈtuː.

passage.text: Third, pause after each key point, so that the audience has time to think.
passage.reading: ˈθɜːrd, ˈpɔːz ˈæftər ˈiːtʃ ˈkiː ˈpɔɪnt, soʊ ðæt ði ˈɔːdiəns ˈhæz ˈtaɪm tə ˈθɪŋk.

passage.text: Fourth, look at the audience, not at the screen.
passage.reading: ˈfɔːrθ, ˈlʊk ət ði ˈɔːdiəns, ˈnɑːt ət ðə ˈskriːn.

passage.text: If you look at people's faces, they will feel that you are talking to them.
passage.reading: ɪf juː ˈlʊk ət ˈpiːpəlz ˈfeɪsɪz, ðeɪ wɪl ˈfiːl ðæt juː ər ˈtɔːkɪŋ tə ðɛm.

passage.text: Finally, remember that everyone gets nerves before a presentation, even experienced speakers.
passage.reading: ˈfaɪnəli, rɪˈmɛmbər ðæt ˈɛvriwʌn ˈɡɛts ˈnɜːrvz bɪˈfɔːr ə ˌprɛzənˈteɪʃən, ˈiːvən ɪkˈspɪriənst ˈspiːkərz.

passage.text: Take a few deep breaths, smile, and start slowly.
passage.reading: ˈteɪk ə ˈfjuː ˈdiːp ˈbrɛθs, ˈsmaɪl, ənd ˈstɑːrt ˈsloʊli.

passage.text: The audience wants you to succeed.
passage.reading: ði ˈɔːdiəns ˈwɑːnts juː tə səkˈsiːd.

passage.text: Good luck, and let me know how it goes!
passage.reading: ˈɡʊd ˈlʌk, ənd ˈlɛt miː ˈnoʊ ˈhaʊ ɪt ˈɡoʊz!
